title: World War I
aliases: The War To End All Wars
description: Global conflict centered in Europe that introduced industrial-scale warfare and reshaped empires, borders, and international diplomacy.

title: World War II
description: Worldwide war involving the Axis and Allies that resulted in massive casualties, the Holocaust, atomic bombings, and the onset of the Cold War.

title: French Revolution
description: Radical social and political upheaval that ended the Bourbon monarchy, advanced republicanism, and reshaped European politics.

title: The Cold War
description: Geopolitical rivalry between the United States and the Soviet Union marked by ideological conflict, nuclear arms race, and proxy wars.

title: The Industrial Revolution
description: Transition to mechanized manufacturing and new energy sources, dramatically increasing productivity and transforming societies.

title: The American Revolution
description: Colonial revolt against British rule leading to U.S. independence and the creation of a constitutional republic.

title: Meiji Restoration
description: Political revolution that restored imperial rule in Japan and accelerated rapid modernization, industrialization, and Western-style reforms, transforming Japan into a major world power.

title: World War II — European Theater
description: European campaigns of WWII including Blitzkrieg, the Eastern Front, D-Day, and the fall of Berlin, culminating in Germany’s surrender.

title: World War II — Pacific Theater
description: Pacific and Asian fronts of WWII from Pearl Harbor through island-hopping campaigns, Midway, and atomic bombings, ending with Japan’s surrender.

title: The Fall of the Berlin Wall
description: The destruction of the Berlin Wall in 1989, symbolizing the end of the Cold War and leading to German reunification.

title: The Moon Landing
description: The first human landing on the Moon by Apollo 11, a major milestone in the Space Race.

title: The Space Race
description: Cold War competition between the US and USSR to achieve superior spaceflight capability, culminating in the Moon landing.

title: The Cuban Missile Crisis
description: 13-day confrontation between the US and the USSR over Soviet ballistic missiles deployed in Cuba.

title: The Great Depression
description: Severe worldwide economic depression that began in 1929 and lasted until the late 1930s.

title: The Russian Revolution
description: Political and social revolution that abolished the Russian monarchy and established the Soviet Union.

title: The Black Death
description: Pandemic that devastated Eurasia and North Africa, killing tens of millions and reshaping social, economic, and religious life across Europe and beyond.

title: The Renaissance
description: Cultural rebirth emphasizing humanism, classical learning, and artistic innovation, transforming European art, science, and thought.

title: Invention of the Printing Press
description: Gutenberg’s movable-type printing enabled mass reproduction of texts, accelerating literacy, religion, and scientific exchange.

title: The Age of Exploration
description: Period of extensive overseas exploration by European powers, opening global trade routes and initiating widespread cultural, biological, and economic exchanges.

title: The Opium Wars
description: Two mid‑19th century conflicts between Qing China and Western powers led by Britain over trade, sovereignty, and opium, reshaping China's foreign relations.

title: First Opium War
description: Conflict between Qing China and Britain sparked by opium suppression and trade disputes; ended with the Treaty of Nanjing.

title: Second Opium War
description: Renewed conflict involving Britain and France against Qing China; culminated in the Convention of Beijing and expanded treaty rights.

title: The Reformation
description: Religious movement challenging Catholic authority that led to the rise of Protestant churches, reshaping European religion, politics, and society.

title: Thirty Years’ War
description: Pan‑European conflict rooted in religious and political rivalries, devastating Central Europe and ending with the Peace of Westphalia.

title: The Counter‑Reformation
description: Catholic Church reform movement responding to Protestantism, defined by the Council of Trent and new religious orders like the Jesuits.

title: The Scientific Revolution
description: Transformative period in European science emphasizing observation, mathematics, and experimentation, laying foundations for modern science.

title: The Enlightenment
description: Intellectual movement advancing reason, individual rights, and skepticism of authority, influencing revolutions and modern institutions.

title: Treaty of Westphalia (1648)
description: Series of treaties ending the Thirty Years’ War, recognizing state sovereignty and non‑intervention within the Holy Roman Empire.

title: The Glorious Revolution (1688)
description: Overthrow of James II leading to constitutional monarchy and parliamentary supremacy in England; influenced Enlightenment political thought.

title: The English Civil War (1642–1651)
description: Series of conflicts between Royalists and Parliamentarians over sovereignty, religion, and taxation; ended with Parliament’s victory and the execution of Charles I.

title: Restoration of the Monarchy (1660)
description: Return of Charles II and re‑establishment of the English monarchy after the Interregnum, recalibrating relations among Crown, Church, and Parliament.

title: Bill of Rights (1689)
description: Act establishing limits on monarchy and rights of Parliament; foundation for constitutional monarchy and a model for later rights documents.
